verdicts.note: Refers to self vs 'the males'; study of women students confirms female.
'normal, basic school' plus her own 'Oh no' to all-girls question supports mixed-sex; medium fine.
States course is industrial design and technology -> D&T.
Past first year, placement (sandwich) pending -> Year 2; inferential, medium ok.
Father is engineer/Project Manager -> family member in the industry.
Mother steered her toward industrial design -> agree with mother's encouragement.
Father informed but did not explicitly encourage study; neither-agree justified, low conf ok.
Careers advisors 'never said that much' -> disagree with advisor encouragement.
Breadth was a factor (via mother's reasoning) but 'strongly' not warranted by quote -> agree.
'didn't quite realise how much technology' -> chose with little knowledge of content.
'get your foot in the door' -> degree valuable even if not entering profession.
No one described as discouraging; family steered toward -> no.
'did really enjoy that' -> drawn by interest/enjoyment.
'some aspects I hate but... some I do like... change day to day' -> neither/ambivalent.
'really difficult... really hard' vs prior assurances -> harder than expected, strongly agree.
'very much like brain storming' -> very satisfied with group work.
'gained more confidence... through group work' -> course develops interpersonal skills.
Never talks to tutor, not beneficial; tutors not approachable -> dissatisfied.
'they just lecture... not bothered if you understand' -> dissatisfied with lecturer support.
Enjoyed the open design/research board project -> satisfied with design work; medium ok.
'I hated that part' (workshop/machining) -> dissatisfied with practical work.
'good course... very varied' is positive but 'very satisfied' overstates -> satisfied.
Electronics helper 'helps the females more' -> females get more help, agree.
'I've applied to [company]' and intends more -> yes.
'money (laughs)' names money as a good thing but jokey, no 'need' stated -> downgrade to medium.
'getting a break from the course' -> break from education.
'it'll help you in your job if you've had work experience' -> values work experience.
'that's what they look for' (employability) -> placement improves job chances; overlaps experien but distinct.
'feel a bit older because more experience' -> personal development/maturity.
Quote is 'fresher perspective... more skills'; never mentions grades -> over-reach for grade-improvement item.
'a lot are very technical which I obviously don't want' -> available work doesn't appeal.
Item is 'could NOT find placement in suitable location'; she intends to go and only states a distance preference -> not supported (belongs to location).
Brainstorming product ideas / arty / textiles design -> design work.
Managerial-vs-specialised prompt -> 'be more specialised' = technical/specialist.
Teaching named only as a job fallback ('if I can't find anything else'); no expressed desire for further study -> inference not in text.
Explicitly says 'I'll probably teach' -> if further study, PGCE/teaching is the area; low conf appropriate.
'want to be in travelling distance' -> location important; correct home for this quote.
